summary: Red team of the accepted library audit AUDIT-13 (five roadmaps: AdelicAlgebraicGroups, AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights, ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces, AutomorphicBundles and AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups). Every one of the 227 cited declarations exists at the pinned commits and says what its note claims; every layer verdict follows from its targets, and no verdict changes. 54 findings: 1 high, 18 medium, 35 low. The high one: AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.1 and the summary say that no topology on G(𝔸) exists in either library, but Mathlib topologizes the points Hom(A, R) of every affine scheme over a topological ring (CommRingCat.HomTopology, Mathlib/Algebra/Category/Ring/Topology.lean:50, with functoriality, closed embeddings for closed subschemes and embeddings for fibre products) and makes GL_n(R), SL_n(R) and Rˣ topological groups, so GL_n(𝔸), SL_n(𝔸) and the ideles are already topological groups. The medium ones are mostly library material the notes deny or leave out: the classical SL₂(ℤ) reduction theory (fundamental domain, Siegel-set bound, finitely many cusps, finite volume), Mathlib's proper-action and covering-map results and Tau Ceti's groupoid equivalences for ALS.0–ALS.3, associated-bundle operations (pullback, Hom and alternating bundles, tensor products of line bundles), the Lie algebra of a Lie group, lieExp, Ad and Lie subalgebras of closed subgroups, smooth functions on Lie groups, the idele class group as the GL₁ adelic quotient, and a statable finite-flat condition at p = 2; and duplicate records that miss owners elsewhere (Tau Ceti ModularForms layers 2 and 10C, ModularCurvesPartII R14.1, LieGroups layers 5, 7 and 9, GeometricTopology layer 1, the Deligne–Serre lifting lemma), plus one layer (ALS.5) audited against the wrong targets.

findings.claim: The classical SL₂/ℚ case of reduction theory is in the libraries and is not cited anywhere in AUDIT-13. Mathlib proves that every point of ℍ is SL₂(ℤ)-equivalent to a point of the standard domain 𝒟, that 𝒟 lies in the Siegel set {|x| ≤ 1/2, y ≥ √3/2}, that only finitely many explicit g satisfy z, g•z ∈ 𝒟 (the Siegel finiteness property), that truncations of 𝒟 are compact, and that every arithmetic subgroup of GL₂(ℝ) has finitely many cusp orbits (so finitely many Siegel sets at any level). Tau Ceti proves that 𝒟 has finite invariant volume and that 𝒟ᵒ (and its coset tiling) is a measure-theoretic fundamental domain for PSL₂(ℤ) and any subgroup. Mathlib also has the GL₂(ℝ)-invariant measure on ℍ, an invariant measure on a quotient by a non-normal, non-discrete closed subgroup. Via the SL₂ strong approximation that AA.4 already cites, SL₂(ℚ)\SL₂(𝔸)/SL₂(ℤ̂)SO(2) is SL₂(ℤ)\ℍ, so these are the classical form of the SL₂/ℚ case. This is the same standard the review applied to AA.4 when it upgraded strong approximation to `partial` on the strength of SL₂(ℤ) → SL₂(ℤ/dℤ).
